title: GPU OOM + CUDA driver mismatch debug notes
content:
Purpose: scratchpad for investigating repeated CUDA OOMs and some driver/runtime mismatch symptoms seen on staging GPUs (g4dn, A100 pools). Notes are messy - collecting commands tried, error snippets, hypotheses, and next steps.

Symptoms observed:
- Intermittent "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate X MiB" when serving large context prompts (~16k tokens).
- On some containers get: "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version" during import or when instantiating model.
- Occasional "cuDNN error: CUDNN_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED" during first forward pass.
- Container logs: "failed to initialize NVML: Shared library not found" after recent base image change.

Environment snapshot (when issue reproduced):
- nvidia-smi output (host):
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  | NVIDIA-SMI 470.199.02   Driver Version: 470.199.02   CUDA Version: 11.4     |
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
- container pip list / torch info (conda env):
  torch==2.2.0+cu117
  torchvision==0.15.2
  torchaudio==2.2.0
  cudatoolkit (conda) 11.7
- nvcc --version (host/container if present): shows CUDA 11.7 toolkit on build node.

Hypothesis 1: driver/runtime mismatch
- Host driver 470.x officially supports up to CUDA 11.4; container has libraries built for cu117 (11.7). That explains "driver version is insufficient" and some symbol errors (cublasLt or newer cuBLAS symbols missing).
- Repro steps: try importing torch inside container, see explicit error: "libcublas.so.11: undefined symbol: cublasLtCreate" or "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version".
- Quick repro command used: python -c "import torch; print(torch.version.cuda); print(torch.cuda.is_available())"
  Output in failing case: 11.7, False + driver mismatch warning.

Hypothesis 2: OOM from batching + KV cache + half precision issues
- Model tokenization + generation path keeps KV cache in GPU memory; effective memory per request > expected.
- Mixed bsz/seq distribution: tail requests with long contexts cause single-request to OOM.
- FP16 transient allocations (amp/autocast) can cause fragmentation leading to OOM even when nominal free memory seems sufficient.

Commands tried and results:
- nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY: shows top-level memory usage by process; helped identify that previous model process (zombie) still held 20% GPU.
- docker run --gpus all --runtime=nvidia -v /var/run/nvidia:/var/run/nvidia ... -> earlier base images were missing libnvidia-ml.so in expected paths -> error: "failed to initialize NVML: Shared library not found". Fixed by ensuring --gpus and nvidia-container-toolkit on host and mounting /usr/lib/nvidia.
- ldd $(python -c 'import torch; import os; print(os.path.dirname(torch.__file__))')/lib/libtorch_cuda.so -> revealed missing libcublasLt symbol when host driver too old.
- conda install cudatoolkit=11.4 into environment -> reduced driver mismatch errors but then runtime expects cu114 and some wheels built for cu117 still failing. Concluded mixing conda cudatoolkit and pip wheel builds is messy.

Workarounds attempted: what helped and what didn't
- Reduce batch size / reduce seq length -> mitigated OOM in many cases (good temporary).
- Set TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA=1 (experimental) -> no effect for our builds.
- export CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 to get better stack traces -> helped find offending operator.
- Set max_split_size_mb in torch.cuda memory allocator (torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction / set_max_split_size_mb) -> slight improvement for fragmentation but not solve.
- Use model.eval() + with torch.no_grad() aggressively in serving path -> reduces peak allocations.
- Replace fp16 + autocast with fp32 for suspect endpoints -> increased memory but eliminated some unstable out-of-memory crashes (tradeoff).
- Restarted GPU daemon / host NVIDIA driver update to 515.86 -> after updating driver to >=515, containers with cu117-based wheels stopped complaining about driver mismatch (still some OOMs due to load).

Error snippets observed: (copied raw)
- "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.75 GiB (GPU 0; 15.90 GiB total capacity; 13.20 GiB already allocated)"
- "OSError: libcublas.so.11: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory"
- "RuntimeError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered" (happened once, likely invalid indexing)
- "RuntimeError: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version"

Notes / theories to verify:
- Confirm on all staging hosts: host NVIDIA driver >= 515 when using cu117 wheels. If not, scheduling should prefer nodes with matching drivers or use containers with older CUDA runtime.
- Avoid mixing conda cudatoolkit with pip wheels - prefer conda-forge/pip consistent stack or rebuild wheels for target CUDA.
- For long-context generation, add adaptive batching that caps sequence length or routes long requests to dedicated large-GPU instances (A100) to avoid OOM on smaller GPUs.

Next steps (actionable):
1) Add a node-level check that reports: host driver, nvidia-smi CUDA reported version, and compatible CUDA versions for installed driver. Put check into node-exporter / fleet health. (blocked by infra change request INF-2389).
2) For serving-runtime: add explicit assertion at startup that torch.cuda.is_available() is True and torch.version.cuda is compatible with host driver; log clear guidance if mismatch.
3) Implement a temporary routing rule in staging to avoid scheduling cu117 containers on nodes with driver < 515. (Coord with platform team).
4) Add more aggressive pre-checks in container entrypoint: ldd on libtorch_cuda.so to surface missing native libs early and fail fast.
5) Track OOM frequency per model/route and add automatic fallback to smaller model or truncated context when memory pressure detected.

Reference commands I re-ran today: 
- nvidia-smi
- docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:11.7-base nvidia-smi
- python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__, torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.is_available())"
- ldconfig -p | grep cublas
- ldd /opt/conda/lib/python3.8/site-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so | grep "not found"

Open questions / items for followup:
- Do we have an internal doc listing which driver versions are deployed on each node pool? If yes, link it to scheduler so we can gate container images.
- Investigate whether NCCL version mismatches produce subtle instability under load (seen some NCCL warnings in logs).
- Decide long-term: enforce a minimum driver in AMI bake pipeline or build wheels for older CUDA to preserve compatibility with older nodes.

Quick TL;DR: Most immediate root cause was driver/runtime mismatch on some nodes (driver too old for cu117 wheels). OOMs also legit in high-tail latency long-context requests; mitigated by reducing request size, improving batching and updating drivers. Next: gate images by driver compatibility and add startup checks.

Raw snippets/logs attached (copied in-line above) and added links to INF-2389 / GH issue for follow-ups.
